items.body: Decision record for issue #5801 (decomposition item 3 of parent #5672), written in the #5900 precedent shape (PR #7877). Task 14235. ## What it settles - **Share shape:** per-share key, two modes recorded in the share manifest — readable (grantees receive the key) and sealed (peers store/forward ciphertext, hold no key). - **Key holders & delivery:** owner always; readable grantees hold the current epoch key; keys delivered wrapped to identity keys via the group scheme's welcome machinery; delegation mints a new share, never a key hand-off; group keys are not share keys. - **Rotation:** event-driven epochs (add/remove/revoke/mode-change/owner) reusing pkgs/id/src/encryption's N7 discipline — no timer rotation; lazy re-encryption. - **Revocation:** forward-only cryptographic take-back is the v1 promise (answers the parent's open question); sealed shares get complete take-back; retroactive unreadability of delivered readable epochs is explicitly not promised. - **Recipient proofs:** owner-signed share manifest (grant lineage, granted-set commitment, epoch, classification ceiling, expiry) — provenance, integrity, completeness-within-the-grant; nothing provable about ungranted objects (existence privacy symmetry). - **Composition:** classification ∩ grant ∩ mode, each layer only narrowing; classification may mandate sealed mode. Alternatives rejected and the invariants implementation must hold are in the record. No parent #5672 decision is changed; boundaries with #5799 / #5802 / #5803 stated in §7. Closes #5801 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: Decision record: public shares through ID — discovery, limits, unpublish semantics (#5802)
items.body: Decision record for #5802 (from #5672), produced by queue task 22717. Docs only; no implementation. **Done-check first:** #5802 read in full (body + all comments); main searched — no public-shares decision record exists (confirmed independently by task 21850's second-pass verdict, 2026-11-24). All coordination inputs are now closed with records landed (#5672, #5799, #5800, #5803, #5806), so the design is written against fixed inputs. **Decisions taken (D1–D5):** - **D1** — A public share is a *public grant*: an ordinary #5799 grant whose subject is the well-known public principal, created by an explicit atomic publish action (grant + publication record + manifest). Unguessable share identifier; no delegation; classification ceiling enforced per object at publish and at each update emission. - **D2 — Discovery:** unlisted by default (link-only), listed by per-share opt-in in the owner's public listing; **no global directory** in v1. The #5801 share manifest (minus key material) is adopted as the public share's provenance/integrity artifact and discovery payload — answering the question #5801 §7 explicitly left to this record. Unlisted is labelled honestly as obscurity, not access control. - **D3 — Limits:** `read` only, plus optional `subscribe`; `write`/`append` can never be public in v1. Mandatory three-layer serving limits (per-share, per-owner aggregate, receiving-side per #5800) with stated v1 starting defaults as configuration, not invariants; caps fail loudly, never silently truncate. - **D4 — Public Turso:** publication names foreign collections explicitly (later tables are not auto-published); reads served through the #5806 adapter's read path with a server-side read-only credential or a declared materialized replica — the owner's credential never reaches readers; grant restriction pushed into the source query per #5803. - **D5 — Unpublish:** unpublish *is* grant revocation — serving, listing, and manifest stop at the next authorization check; hosted replicas retracted via #5800 scope-exit; the identifier then returns the indistinguishable-absence outcome (existence privacy re-attaches). Forward-only honesty boundary stated verbatim for publish-time UX. Re-publication mints a new identifier; dead links are never resurrected or redirected. Publication record retained owner-side only for accounting. Plus 8 implementation invariants, rejected alternatives with reasons, and an explicit divergence check: the one deliberate scoping (existence privacy is suspended by the owner for the published slice only, and re-attaches at unpublish) is recorded as a scoping of the parent rule, not a change to it; no parent decision is amended. **Reserved for Drewry (one item, §6):** whether public shares are also served to fully anonymous no-identity readers via a public web gateway — a product/platform commitment, not a protocol question. Interim default recorded so implementation is not blocked: v1 serves ID peers only; a later gateway would be an additive front-end changing no rule in the record. Left **unmerged** for Felix's review. #5802 stays open until this record merges, per its acceptance. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: id-grants: publish and unpublish for public shares (#14781)
items.body: Before: a public grant could exist in `id-grants`, but there was no publish action, no publication record and no share manifest, so nothing tied a public share's grant, record and link together or kept dead links dead. After: `id_grants::publication` holds the owner's publish and unpublish actions from the #5802 record (D1, D2.3, D5). Publish checks everything first, then creates the public grant and the `PublicationRecord` together; the `ShareManifest` is derived from the live record. Unpublish revokes the grant and retires the record together, keeping it on the owner's audit surface. An unpublished or expired identifier resolves exactly like one that never existed, an identifier is never minted twice (even after the audit record is purged), and a `ClassLevel` ceiling refuses above-ceiling objects at publish time and gates each emission. The publish-time copy for the forward-only boundary and the unlisted label are exported as constants. How: a pure module with no I/O. Share identifiers are minted from caller-supplied entropy, so the host supplies a cryptographic random source. Manifest signing belongs to the #5801 manifest work and is not done here. `tests/publication.rs` covers atomic publish, refusal leaving nothing behind, unpublish, dead links, listing, expiry and the classification gate. Fixes #14781 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(id): partial replication protocol decision record (#5800)
items.body: Decision record for #5800 (task 16841, lane any-d), the partial replication protocol design gated until now on the #5799 grants model (closed, record posted 2026-11-05). **Settles:** (1) subset snapshot — grant-evaluated at the cut by the #5678/#5799 resolver, self-describing (grant id + snapshot epoch), manifest lists included objects only, chunked transfer with (grant, epoch, chunk) resume so snapshot_once retries stay in the same transfer; (2) scoped updates — per-grant epoch-ordered stream, membership re-evaluated at each emission, tombstones for deletes vs reason-free scope-exit markers, resync only by fresh snapshot of the current scope; (3) existence privacy by construction — scope-only content, no totals/progress counts, absent ≡ ungranted, per #5672 and #5799 invariant 6; (4) dangling references — redacted placeholders with per-grant keyed tokens (linkable within a slice, opaque across grants), omission only where a data type schema marks a reference optional, closure only under an explicit grant flag (never implicit, per #5799 invariant 3). **Also in the record:** six rejected alternatives with reasons, nine implementation invariants, receiving-side cap/pause/drop behaviour, and an explicit divergence check against #5672/#5799 — none: parents consumed as fixed inputs, new mechanics sit in the space #5799 left to #5800. No further splits filed (neighbours #5801/#5802 already exist). Design only; implementation timing is a separate decision per the issue. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): talk-page semantics decision record (closes #5871)
items.body: Closes #5871. Decision record for talk-page semantics, settling the four questions #5682 §2 leaves open. Design only — no implementation code. **Decisions** 1. **Creation — lazy.** A talk page exists only as the `talk_for` binding on the first signed post; an undiscussed object costs zero storage and exposes no artifact. Clients may offer "start the discussion" to any object reader; nothing is pre-created. 2. **Permissions — intersection, narrowing-only.** `can_read(talk_page) = can_read(object) ∧ is_member(conversation)`. No override may widen past object read-authority. Cross-object threads intersect over *all* anchors. Hard rule: no content **or existence** leak — for a non-reader the page is indistinguishable from an object with no talk page. 3. **Lifecycle.** Archive makes posting fail at admission (architectural, not client-side); ownership transfer moves binding/governance authority with the object without re-binding; object tombstone **preserves** the conversation, folds the binding to `orphaned`, removes the object-side entry point, and never re-adopts the page on object re-creation; `talk_for` targeting a conversation is rejected so recursion is depth one. 4. **Moderation and binding — split.** Object owner governs structure (lock/close/pin/announce/slow) via signed events; server moderation (#835) retains takedown, implemented as signed events, never deletes. Only the object owner or an owner-named delegate may bind; unauthorized bindings are rejected at admission (disputed is for legitimate conflicts only). 5. **Mapping to existing code.** Membership is the object read set projected through group policy (`pkgs/id/src/groups/policy.rs`); `History::Full` for unconditional audiences, `History::FromJoin` when read-authority is granted per key, `Recent(n)` only to tighten. Revocation cannot un-deliver — stated as the design's one honest limitation, with key rotation left to #5801. **Explicitly recorded for parents/siblings:** #5682 §2 is preserved and only refined (the read-authority sentence is read as intersection + narrowing); #5872 is unchanged — this record supplies the binding authority and visibility intersection it delegated; #5870/#835/#5873/#5874/#5875 untouched. If #5682 intended "any object reader reads every thread regardless of membership", that is a parent change and is flagged rather than made silently. Nine testable invariants are in §6 (intersection at read time, no-existence-leak indistinguishability, narrowing-only as a property test, lazy equivalence, depth one, preservation, authority determinism, architectural archive, total history mapping). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(id): design jurisdiction-aware hosted user stores
items.body: ## Summary ```text signup → authoritative jurisdiction → restricted user store + local bucket migration → fence → export/import → verify → CAS switch → safe cleanup ``` Designs #2283 and links implementation follow-ons #3399, #3400, #3401, #3402, #3403, and #3404. Deployment support and residency guarantees remain subject to #2285. ## Evidence - **Before:** #2283 had no concrete routing or migration design. - **After:** Design covers its seven requirements, failure modes, a single-account runbook, and implementation slices; `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit. Documentation only; no runtime tests. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way **Blast Radius:** documentation Proposed design only; production enablement is explicitly gated on account-level verification. --- Need help on this PR?
